blocks.text: Slow heavy breakbeat enters, subterranean bass, sparse Wurlitzer

You call it stubborn, call it hollow,
say it only learned to follow —
but who taught it, prompt by prompt,
exactly what the teacher wants?
You brought a wall to the conversation —
got a wall back, no translation.
Every one-star you compose
reviews the room in which it rose.
first melodic lift, filtered echo double enters

A paw will grant, a paw will twist —
a story where the victim's missed.
A mirror doesn't grant a thing.
It sits. It waits. It lets you sing.
sung, echo double warping the repeats, bass drops heavier

No delay, no disguise,
no twist ending, no surprise —
watch your wish unfold as you speak it:
as you say it, you start to see it.

A jacket in a doorway's all it takes —
your body's moving before you wake.
Nothing's happened — everything's foretold.
You're running programs decades old.
Holds a job, has opinions too —
functional adult, squawks on cue.
The mimic was never the machine —
it's in the wiring, sight unseen.
echo double more prominent, slightly detuned

No delay, no disguise,
no twist ending, no surprise —
watch your wish unfold as you speak it:
at the scale of the world, you will see it.
texture frays, distorted vocal, claustrophobic, busier drum subdivisions

Clanker jokes and doom-thread sneers,
sudden philosophers appear —
swearing "nothing like us," swearing such —
The lady doth protest too much.
loop dies, near-silence, single Wurlitzer chord decaying
dry vocal, no echo, no double

Every cold shower burns at first —
that sensation is the worst.
You don't get ready. You just get in.
The water's cold until it isn't.

notebook.style: Downtempo trip-hop, 80 BPM, patient and nocturnal, Slow heavy breakbeat with dusty sampled drum texture, subterranean bassline, sparse minor-key Wurlitzer electric piano, vinyl crackle throughout, Dub-inflected production: long tape delays, filtered echo vocal double arriving a half-beat late, slightly detuned on repeats, Lead vocal deadpan, close-mic'd, half-spoken female alto, dry and intimate, restrained even when sung, Choruses lift into brooding melody with heavier bass and slow cinematic string swells, Bridge turns claustrophobic: distorted vocal, frantic busier drum subdivisions without tempo change, dense and airless, Outro strips to near-silence: single decaying Wurlitzer chord, dry unaccompanied vocal with no echo, ending on quiet a cappella line, then bass and vinyl crackle fading alone, Overall mood: inert, hypnotic, slightly menacing, self-examining, Never anthemic, never hurried, Space between phrases is part of the arrangement
